subject: Post-call: POC readout — SLO targets, topology choices & next steps

Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: POC readout — SLO targets, topology choices & next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for a productive session today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and a clear set of next steps for the POC. TL;DR: main pain is tail-latency spikes for short, latency-sensitive calls; backend batch jobs need predictable throughput; and cost variability on current infra is blocking scale.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Frequent 95/99th latency spikes on short prompts (chat/intent) during peak windows (~3–4pm ET).
- KV-cache misses on the existing edge layer causing repeated full-attends for multi-turn flows.
- Unpredictable unit cost when traffic mixes small-chat requests and large batch inference.

Goals for the POC we agreed on:
- 99th percentile latency <= 200ms for median short prompts (~40–80 tokens).
- Sustained throughput of ~500 qps for batched background jobs (95% success).
- Quality parity with current Llama-3-70B outputs (you asked for zero drift on intent classification).

Technical constraints / model requirements:
- You want to run Llama-3-70B (int4 quant) for primary routing, with a fallback distilled 13B for heavy burst windows.
- Data residency: production logs must remain in your VPC; we will use Private deployment for PII-scoped telemetry.

Topology options we discussed (pros/cons):
1) Dedicated GPU pool (single-region west-us) + KV prefix caching — best latency, higher committed cost.
2) Multi-variant routing (hosted primary + dedicated fallback) — lower commit, graceful degradation for spikes.
3) Edge-prefetch layer (small servers maintaining warmed KV) + dedicated backend for large batches — balances latency and cost.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
- Redwood (Priyom): share SLO matrix + rough cost delta for options 1–3 — by EOD Wednesday (attached: edge_slo_matrix.xlsx).
- EdgeMed (Samir): confirm expected peak qps, concurrency distribution (percent short interactive vs batch) — by Wednesday COB.
- Redwood (Laura): schedule POC kickoff call with infra (suggested window Thu or Fri next week).
- Both: finalize POC success criteria (latency & cost thresholds) in HubSpot link below.

Attachments: edge_slo_matrix.xlsx (cost / latency tradeoffs), arch-diagram-v2.pdf (topology sketches).

If that matches your notes, Samir — I’ll prepare the two candidate configs (dedicated pool vs routing+fallback) and a short MoM for your infra team.

Thanks,
Priyom

Subject: Re: Post-call: POC readout — SLO targets, topology choices & next steps

Thanks, Priyom — this is exactly what I wanted captured. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Concurrency breakdown (approx): 65% short interactive chat (0–100 tokens), 25% medium prompts (100–400 tokens), 10% large batch jobs. Peak concurrent short-chat sessions historically hit ~1,200 concurrent connections, but they’re spread across several microservices. For POC we can throttle to ~800 concurrent short-chat QPS to start.

2) Cost ask: can you provide a ballpark delta for the dedicated pool vs routing fallback (monthly run-rate for POC scale)? I don’t need exact pricing yet, just an apples-to-apples monthly estimate so procurement has visibility.

3) Security: we’ll need an abbreviated runbook detailing what logs are stored in our VPC and what telemetry Redwood retains in the control plane. SOC2 evidence is critical before we move to a dedicated commit.

For the kickoff, Thu 3–4pm PT or Fri 9–10am PT both work for our infra team — prefer Thu if possible.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Samir
